# XY08: 海晏堂 Haiyan Tang, "Hall of Peaceful Seas"

3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=XY08` · Page: `/xiyanglou#XY08` · Row: `research/buildings/XY08-haiyan-tang/`

## What it was

The largest of the group. Basically finished by 1759 as 水法殿十一间楼; the board 海晏堂 hung only from 1781 (S310). It faced west with 11 bays on two levels, and two great stairs curved down to the pool, where cast copper animal heads on seated stone figures, six each side, spouted water: the water clock of the twelve hours (S02 p.153, S258 p.182, S823). Behind it an H-shaped block held Benoist's machines and the reservoir 锡海 of 27.36 × 5.92 × 1.44 m (S109; S06 for the width; depth S600) between two raised waterwheel houses, with zig-zag stairs at the east end; side fronts of 13 bays make a run of about 105 m (S02 p.155, S593, S604 through S415). In 1786 Bourgeois says that men carried water to fill "the immense basin of the château d'eau" before the emperor's visits, the machine having worn out (S258 p.166); he names no building, and this may or may not be this tank. In 1795 the disused machines were ordered reused as metal and timber (S600).

## After 1860

Burned in October 1860. In 1873 Ohlmer photographed the west and north fronts still up to the parapet. The brick casing of the reservoir block, up to 5 m thick, was stripped over time and the block collapsed in the 1940s, leaving the rammed earth core (S593, S110). A dig of about 2015 found the waterwheel rooms and drains; 800 m² in a search extract (S310). The core was conserved about 2016-17 (S110, S821). Seven of the twelve heads are held in China today: ox, tiger, monkey and boar at the Poly Art Museum, horse at the park since 2020, rat and hare at the National Museum since 2013. The whereabouts of dragon, snake, goat, rooster and dog are unknown (S817, S822); one reprint repeats an unconfirmed report of the dragon head in Taiwan (S823). Which heads are held where: S822, S823, S815.

## Open questions

- **Q2. What is S01: the original or the tracing?** Malone bought both (S02 p.231). The museum's "1920s" is its own cataloguing and rests on the provenance line. Evidence for the tracing (the maps worker's inference, medium to high confidence, not proven): his plates p.72 and p.99 (S23) show a flap folded over the Back L
- **Q4. The pasted slips.** Malone names slips at 九洲清晏 (p.72 caption, p.80 note) and 如意馆, group 40 (p.96 note; App. II). A footnote nearby was first read as being about Qichun: it is not. **None is on this copy at those places.** One slip is seen, at 海晏堂 (Q2). If the flat paper hides a slip, or if the tracing copied only
- **Q16. 海晏堂's east half and the plan's working names.** S01 writes 黄花灯 (黄花阵), 转马台 (线法山), 线法画 (线法墙), 西水?房. Its 海晏堂 has three parts that map poorly onto the plates' single mass. 线法画 has 6 walls per side on S01, Malone says 5, `params.json` 7 pairs.
- **Q32. OSM errors.** 线法画 (west of 方河), 养雀笼, possibly 映水兰香; 蓄水楼 point at 116.3055 is 海晏堂's reservoir, not XY02; 谐奇趣's point is 23 m from the ruin. Used only as a hint. Positions come from S01 for all but rows noted `S03`.
- **Q56. Reconstructions against the period evidence.** None of these changes a row; all are for the detailed models. 上下天光 YM08: the album reads as asymmetrical, while the dig found two identical symmetrical foundations and a 乾隆 archive says two hexagonal pavilions (S505, S152): for 1860 the album may be out of date. Xiy
- **Q59. Twin claims to hold loosely.** 海晏堂 follows the Grand Trianon: Beurdeley 1971 p.68, repeated widely; Rabreau (S415 p.81) says its grounds would be sought in vain. No filiation of any Xiyang Lou building to a European print is proved. 安佑宫 YM17 仿寿皇殿 (S05 j.81 f.20b), but that hall had only 3 bays before 1749 (S422)
- **Q64. The plan's scale and turn in this strip (Round 6).** Buildings and pools hold ratio about 1 to surveyed sizes at the local ground scale (0.99 for buildings, n=5; 0.98 for spaces, n=7), so the METHOD's "buildings at another scale" does not hold here, and rows sized by the hall scale run about 15% large. Exception
- **Q70. 海晏堂 (Round 6).** Side fronts: S604 13 bays, 105 m; on plates 11 and 13 that makes a door about 5 m wide and 11 m high, while 13 bays = 39 m gives a door 1.9 x 4.3 m.
